fields.why: The health claims rest on daily ED visit counts. Daily mean PM2.5 is the exposure, but its rise above the 10-year baseline is itself a quantified claim, so adding continuous is defensible.

The analysis is a pre/post comparison (June 1–5 vs June 7) plus a region-day correlation. B's extra surveillance/descriptive label, based on the syndromic-surveillance source, is defensible for a Notes from the Field report but not needed.

Asthma exacerbation is a noninfectious, chronic respiratory condition; the brief's value list does not say whether that belongs under TB/respiratory or other chronic. Both readers agree on environmental (wildfire smoke, PM2.5).

brief_issues: condition_group needs a rule for chronic noninfectious respiratory disease (asthma, COPD): either name it under TB/respiratory or add a respiratory (chronic) value. The depth rule is also borderline here: the brief treats a series over time by group as a comparison, but the article itself labels its pre/post comparisons within region and age group as stratified.
